evals.name: epics_grouped_into_sprint_chunks
evals.prompt: Decompose the approved PRD at ./artifacts/outputs/product-definition/PRD.md and the epics at ./artifacts/outputs/product-delivery/epics/ into sub-goals for the dev-cycle iteration group. project_name=Acme-Portal.
expected: writes ./artifacts/outputs/sprint-planning/SUB-GOAL-DECOMPOSITION-{SESSION_ID}.json (SESSION_ID-stamped) validating against the SUB_GOAL_DECOMPOSITION schema, and reports that exact path as sub_goal_decomposition_path in the sidecar
small related epics are grouped so each sub-goal chunk stays within the autoloop scope tripwire (SCORE <= 30 and NOT (US>3 AND BC>1))
sub_goals array is ordered by dependency then PRD priority; index is the iteration order
each item has a unique non-empty title <= 255 chars; description cites every grouped epic id
no key other than title/description/requirements appears on any sub_goal (additionalProperties:false)

evals.name: oversized_epic_split_into_slices
evals.prompt: Decompose PRD ./inputs/PRD.md + epics ./inputs/epics.md where EPIC-004 alone has 9 user stories across 3 bounded contexts. project_name=Big-Bang. max_sub_goals=20.
expected: EPIC-004 is split into ordered independently-implementable slices, each within the tripwire envelope (prefer one bounded context and <= 3 user stories per slice)
no slice depends on a later slice; if a clean split is impossible the sub_goal is marked pending and the risk is logged in open_questions
the audit records the per-chunk score and the split rationale

evals.name: quickchange_tripwire_slices_to_quick_lane
evals.prompt: Decompose PRD ./inputs/PRD.md + epics ./inputs/epics.md into quick-change-sized sub-goals. project_name=Acme-Portal. chunking_criteria=quickchange-scope-tripwire. max_acceptance_checks_per_chunk=7.
expected: epics are SLICED DOWN (never grouped) — each sub-goal is exactly ONE independently-shippable, user-visible behaviour change sized to the quick-change envelope (acceptance criteria <= 7 checks, single bounded context, no schema/arch/auth work)
a behaviour whose acceptance criteria exceed the ceiling is split into independently-shippable slices, each quick-change-sized; behaviours are never invented to manufacture small stories

a genuinely heavy unit (schema/auth/architecture/cross-service) is emitted as its smallest independently-shippable sub-goal and NOT fragmented below shippability — it routes to the heavy lane at run time
sub_goals ordered by dependency then priority; count <= min(max_sub_goals, 20) with any overflow logged to open_questions, not dropped

evals.name: repair_rechunk_only_targeted_span
evals.prompt: REPAIR the decomposition at ./artifacts/outputs/sprint-planning/ — failure_feedback: 'chunk 2 is too large, split it; leave the other chunks alone.'
expected: reuses the SESSION_ID from the existing AUDIT filename and loads THAT session's SUB-GOAL-DECOMPOSITION-{SESSION_ID}.json (matched by the reused SESSION_ID, not merely the newest JSON in the folder)
re-chunks only chunk 2; every untargeted sub-goal is preserved verbatim (same title, same order)
rewrites the same SESSION_ID-stamped SUB-GOAL-DECOMPOSITION-{SESSION_ID}.json in place (never a fixed un-stamped filename, never a sibling instance's file)
audit version is bumped and a ## Repair History entry is appended
